model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Share-based payments sit inside personnel expenses and are already deducted from the net income the FCFE stream is built from (FY2025 annual report Note 4.3); there is no cash-flow add-back to reverse, so no separate SBC deduction is made. Share count held flat because buybacks are part of the FCFE being valued; charging both would double-count.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: Calendar 2025 buybacks approximated from the fall in shares on issue (796.5m -> 754.9m, FY2024 vs FY2025 NAVPS share counts) at an average ~EUR 50; comprises the FY2024 ordinary buyback plus the first EUR 1bn extraordinary programme and part of the second. Indicative only; FCFE, not the buyback figure, drives the valuation.
inputs.share_count_basis: 730.035m shares used for NAVPS at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 report). Diluted = basic for SG (FY2025 diluted weighted average equals basic, AR line 35781). The EUR 1.5bn extraordinary buyback launched 3 Aug 2026 (~25m shares at ~EUR 60) post-dates the balance sheet and is not netted, because it is funded from the same tangible equity that is still on the 30 June balance sheet; at a price below IV it is accretive, so this is the conservative treatment.
inputs.tangible_equity_note: NTA per share EUR 74.5 x 730.035m shares at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 kpis). Shareholders' equity Group share EUR 71,645m; NAV per share EUR 83.8.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Discount rate is a EUR cost of equity, not a WACC: deposits and debt securities are operating funding for a bank, so the FCFE stream is already post-interest and is capitalised at the cost of equity with net debt held at zero. Base 11.0% = French 10y OAT ~3.4% (2026, spread widened by the political instability) + 1.4 beta x 5.5% ERP, i.e. a ~1pt French-sovereign premium over a generic European bank CoE of ~10%. Bull 10.0% assumes the French spread normalises and SG re-rates with peers; bear 12.5% assumes the sovereign/bank CDS dislocation of late 2025 persists.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable; IFRS 16 lease costs are inside operating expenses and therefore inside the earnings the FCFE is built from.
inputs.nci_treatment: Earnings to ordinary shareholders are taken on the EPS basis, i.e. net income Group share (already net of NCI, chiefly the Komercni banka, BRD and Ayvens minorities) less AT1 coupons and issuance costs charged to equity. FY2025: NI Group share 6,002 vs EPS 6.80 x 776.3m weighted shares = 5,278; the ~724m gap is the AT1 charge.
inputs.fcfe_construction: FCFE = earnings to ordinary shareholders (EPS basis) minus capital retained to fund RWA growth. Retention = RWA growth (~2% p.a., FY2026 guidance maintained at the Sept 2026 CMD) x 13% CET1 target x RWA (~EUR 380bn implied by CET1 capital / 13.2%) = ~EUR 1.0bn p.a. = ~3.5% of revenue. So the engine's ebitda_margin_path is the FCFE margin = earnings-to-common margin minus 3.5pp. FY2025 anchor: 5,278 - ~980 = ~4,300 = last_fcf (vs actual FY2025 distributions of 4,679 incl. EUR 2bn extraordinary funded from disposal-released capital). D&A, capex, cash tax and SBC paths are zero because every one of those items is already inside the post-tax earnings line; wc_capture is zero.
inputs.excess_capital: CET1 13.2% at 30 June 2026 is stated post the EUR 1.5bn extraordinary buyback and sits only ~20bps above the >13% target (~EUR 0.8bn, ~EUR 1/share), so no surplus-capital bridge item is added. Further disposal gains (>75bps flagged from 2025-2026 disposals, partly already crystallised) are upside not in the base.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank -> SKILL.md routes to earnings on tangible book at the cost of equity. Built as an FCFE-at-CoE stream through the Drivers/engine route (same treatment as the folder's other banks: HBAN, STT, NAB.AX, 2016.HK) so the dashboard slider engine and the workbook validate by construction; `model` is labelled so the multiples sanity check uses cost-of-equity rules, not EV/EBITDA. Owner-FCF DCF is NOT used: bank OCF/FCF are meaningless and deposits are not net debt. 'revenue' in the engine is net banking income (FY2025 EUR 27,254m); 'ebitda_margin_path' is the FCFE margin described in fcfe_construction. RESIDUAL-INCOME CROSS-CHECK on TNAV 74.5/share: justified P/TNAV = (ROTE - g)/(CoE - g); base ROTE 12.5% by 2029, g 2%, CoE 11% -> 1.17x -> ~EUR 87; at the FY2026 guided ROTE of ~11% -> 1.0x -> ~EUR 75; bear ROTE 9%, CoE 12.5% -> 0.68x -> ~EUR 51; bull ROTE 14%, CoE 10%, g 2.5% -> 1.53x -> ~EUR 114. The engine scenarios bracket the same range. The market at ~0.8x TNAV with a 12% H1 2026 ROTE is implicitly discounting at ~13-14% or assuming ROTE falls back toward 9-10%; both are the bear case here. Price is the Yahoo Finance chart API regular-session print at inputs.price_as_of (Paris close Friday 23 Oct 2026); refresh_price.py runs after the build.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: CMD Sept 2026 medium-term revenue CAGR (~3% 2026e-2029), bounded by the 4.3% 5yr revenue CAGR and the 5.4% 5yr tangible NAV/share CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.6% 5yr) is 40% below revenue CAGR (4.3%) and far below EPS/earnings CAGRs. For a bank distributing ~50% of earnings plus EUR 2bn+ of extraordinary buybacks, equity growth understates value creation; tangible NAV per share (+5.4% p.a. 5yr, +7.5% FY2024->FY2025) is the better compounding gauge. EPS and earnings 3yr CAGRs are off the depressed FY2022 base (EPS 1.73; EUR 3.3bn of Russia exit and goodwill charges) and are not run-rate growth.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2020 22,113 -> FY2025 27,254; FY2022 28,059 -> FY2025 27,254 (perimeter shrink from disposals). EPS FY2022 1.73 -> FY2025 6.80; FY2020 EPS -1.02 so the 5yr EPS CAGR is undefined. Equity Group share FY2020 61,684 -> FY2025 70,144; FY2022 66,451 -> FY2025 70,144. 'fcf' CAGRs are on earnings to ordinary shareholders (EPS x weighted shares: FY2022 ~1,423 -> FY2025 5,278); the FY2020 figure was negative so the 5yr CAGR is undefined. NTA/share FY2020 54.8 -> FY2025 71.4.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +2.5% (guidance >+2%; H1 +2.4% reported), then ~3% through FY2029 per the CMD, fading to 2%. Earnings-to-common margin 21.0% in FY2026 (H1 2026 actual 21.9%, H2 seasonally softer; implies ROTE ~11.5%, between the ~11% guidance and the 12.0% H1 print), rising to 23% by FY2029 (ROTE ~12.5%, below the 13-14% CMD target to allow for Global Markets normalisation and the French surtax), then 22.5% as the cycle turns. FCFE margin = that minus 3.5pp retention for 2% RWA growth at 13% CET1. CoE 11%, terminal growth 2%.

bull.narrative: CMD delivered: revenue ~4% CAGR to FY2029 (Bernstein, BoursoBank >EUR 300m, Ayvens synergies), cost/income <55%, ROTE 14% by FY2029 and held (earnings-to-common margin 25.5%, FCFE margin 22%). French spread normalises; CoE 10%, terminal growth 2.5%.

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands on guidance (+2% revenue, margin 20% = ROTE ~11%) then a Global Markets downturn plus cost of risk at 40bps and a persistent French surtax/buyback tax take the earnings-to-common margin back to 18% (ROTE ~9%) with revenue flat in real terms. French sovereign/bank CDS dislocation persists: CoE 12.5%, terminal growth 1.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Transformation holds but the market is right to haircut the CMD: ROTE settles ~12.5% rather than 13-14%, revenue grows ~3% to FY2029 then ~2%, and SG distributes everything above a 13% CET1 on 2% RWA growth. Discounted at an 11% EUR cost of equity with a 1pt French-sovereign premium; terminal value at 11.3x FCFE, i.e. ~1.2x tangible book.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2029/2030+ CMD targets (ROTE 13-14% then >15%, cost/income <55%) are met on 4% revenue growth with Bernstein, BoursoBank and Ayvens all contributing, the French spread normalises and SG re-rates to a 10% cost of equity, ~1.5x tangible book.
scenario_narratives.bear: Earnings normalise down: a markets downturn, cost of risk drifting to the top of or above the 25-30bps range, continued French surtaxes, and revenue ex-disposals roughly flat take ROTE back to ~9% against a 12.5% cost of equity, holding the stock near 0.7x tangible book -- roughly where it trades today.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15-25% house range to 30% because the dominant risk (French sovereign/political instability, rated high severity in the Analysis) is outside management's control and SG's revenue is ~38% Global Markets-driven; the Analysis also flags the 2026 Finance Act surtax and buyback tax as live. Bull trimmed to 20%: the CMD targets are credible given the 2023-2026 record of beating every target, but require three integrations (Bernstein, LeasePlan/Ayvens, SG/Credit du Nord) to all land.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A universal bank is valued on the cash it can distribute to ordinary shareholders after keeping capital at the regulatory target, discounted at the cost of equity -- never on owner FCF, EV/EBITDA or net debt, none of which mean anything for a deposit-funded balance sheet. SG's investment case is a profitability inflection (ROTE 2.5% in 2022 -> 10.2% FY2025 -> 12.0% H1 2026) that the market, at ~0.8x tangible book, only partly believes because of French sovereign risk. The model prices that risk explicitly through a 1pt CoE premium and a 30% bear weight rather than by shading the earnings path, so that the gap between base and market is attributable.
key_risks_to_valuation: French sovereign spread / political instability widening SG's CDS and the equity cost of capital; a sovereign stress scenario (S&P, June 2026) would impair senior debt and the equity story with it
Global Markets cyclicality: ~38% of revenue is GBIS; a volatility/issuance drought compresses the earnings-to-common margin by several points quickly
French bank-specific taxation: the 2026 Finance Act surtax extension and buyback tax reduce distributable earnings; further fiscal tightening is plausible given a ~5% of GDP deficit
Execution across Bernstein consolidation, Ayvens/LeasePlan integration and the SG/Credit du Nord network merger; the base case already assumes ROTE short of the CMD target
Regulatory capital drift: FRTB (Jan 2027) and Basel IV output-floor phase-in could raise RWAs faster than the assumed 2%, increasing retention and cutting FCFE
Cost of risk: modelled inside the 25-30bps guidance in base; a eurozone/French SME downturn to 40-50bps is the bear path

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular-session print at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 52.02-84.82 EUR
data_sources.financials: GLE.PA_Metrics.csv (core_metrics / metrics_normalized, EUR millions) FY2018-FY2025 plus H1 2026; bank KPIs (CET1, ROTE, ROE, cost/income, cost of risk, NAV and NTA per share, NCI, total equity) from the kpis table; FY2025 Universal Registration Document for the EPS-basis share counts and AT1 deduction (lines 2601, 2640, 35779-35786)
